patients.summary: Administrative assistant from India who joins at 51 with six months of breathlessness and is found to have severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with heart failure. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation follows in late 2022 and she is managed on warfarin, furosemide, metoprolol and potassium, with pulmonary hypertension in 2024 and an ICU stay for pulmonary edema in April 2026, after which her mitral valve is opened by balloon commissurotomy in June 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: short of breath, getting worse since around November.

HPI: 51 y/o woman, administrative assistant, originally from India (in the US about ten years), here to establish care. About six months of breathlessness on exertion that has crept up steadily. Now winded after one flight of stairs or a few minutes of brisk walking, which she could do without trouble a year ago. Has started propping herself on extra pillows to sleep and twice a week or so wakes up gasping and has to sit on the edge of the bed for a few minutes. Mild cough, mostly when she lies flat, not productive. No chest pain or pressure. No palpitations. No ankle or leg swelling. No fever.

PMH: rheumatic fever at age 8 (around 1978) in India, hospitalized for it. No monthly or long-term penicillin afterward. No records from that time. No known heart or lung disease.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 11 (1981). Wisdom teeth out age 22 (1992).
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with hypertension, had a stroke at 70. Mother with type 2 diabetes and hypothyroidism. No congenital heart disease or rheumatic fever in the family.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, no drug use. Works full time as an administrative assistant. Lives in Williamsburg.

Exam:
BP 120/75, HR 68 regular, RR 14, T 36.9, SpO2 97% RA. Wt 63.3 kg, Ht 157 cm, BMI 25.7.
Well appearing, speaking full sentences. No JVD at 45 degrees. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles or wheeze. Heart regular. Low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex, heard only after rolling her onto her left side; S1 normal. No other murmurs. Abd soft. No peripheral edema, extremities warm.

ECG (done today, my read): sinus rhythm, normal axis, broad notched P in II and deep terminal negative P in V1 = left atrial enlargement. No ST-T changes.

A/P:
1. Progressive exertional dyspnea with orthopnea and PND, apical diastolic rumble, LAE on ECG, childhood rheumatic fever. Strongly suspect rheumatic mitral stenosis with pulmonary venous congestion. Needs echo.
- TTE ordered, regional hospital echo lab. Scheduled for Mon 5/9.
- CBC, BMP, BNP drawn today.
- Start furosemide 40 mg every morning and potassium chloride ER 20 mEq daily for the congestion. Recheck BMP when she comes back.
- 2 g sodium diet, handout given. Asked her to buy a scale and weigh every morning, write it down.
- Back 5/16 to go over echo. ED for chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fainting.
2. History of rheumatic fever: as above.
3. Health maintenance: records requested from prior primary care office. Will catch up screening and vaccines once I see what she's had.

Reference range: less than 100 pg/mL
Ordering provider: PCP

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Results to patient via portal:
Hi Ms. Rahman, your blood counts are normal (hemoglobin 13.2). Kidney function and potassium are normal (creatinine 0.9, potassium 4.5), good baseline before the water pill. BNP came back 150 (normal is under 100). It is a heart strain marker and the mild rise fits with fluid backing up toward the lungs, which is what we are treating with the furosemide. Echo is Monday. Call or text if anything changes.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Outside records received by fax from patient's previous primary care office (MA), 14 pages, scanned to chart. Abstracted for PCP:
- Problem list there: none active. Rheumatic fever in childhood listed by history.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test 2019: negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV not detected.
- Screening mammogram 2021: BI-RADS 1, negative.
- Immunizations: Pfizer COVID-19 3/18/2021, 4/8/2021, booster 11/20/2021. Influenza 10/9/2021. No Tdap or pneumococcal on file.
- Last seen there in 2021.
Immunizations entered into our record.

reports.text:
Transthoracic echocardiogram, complete 2D with color, spectral and tissue Doppler.
Indication: apical diastolic murmur, exertional dyspnea, history of rheumatic fever.
Rhythm during study: sinus. Image quality: good.

Left ventricle: normal cavity size. Normal wall thickness. Normal systolic function, no regional wall motion abnormality. Ejection fraction 60% (biplane). Left ventricular end-diastolic pressure estimated normal.
Mitral valve: leaflets thickened with restricted excursion and diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet; orifice narrowed. Mitral valve area 1.2 cm² by 2D planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 9 mmHg. No significant mitral regurgitation.
Left atrium: enlarged.
Aortic valve: trileaflet, opens normally. No aortic stenosis or regurgitation.
Right heart: pulmonary artery systolic pressure estimated at 45 mmHg from the tricuspid regurgitant velocity plus estimated right atrial pressure.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Rheumatic mitral stenosis, severe: mitral valve area 1.2 cm² by planimetry, mean gradient 9 mmHg. Enlarged left atrium. Estimated PA systolic pressure 45 mmHg. Normal left ventricular size, wall thickness and systolic function, EF 60%. No significant mitral regurgitation. Normal aortic valve.

documents.title: Echo done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello doctor, I had the heart ultrasound on Monday. The water pill makes me run to the bathroom all morning but I am managing. My weight this week 63 kg every day. Should I keep taking both pills until I see you on Monday the 16th?

documents.title: RE: Echo done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, keep taking both every morning. I have the echo report and want to go through it with you properly in person on Monday, there's a fair bit to explain. Taking the furosemide early in the day like you're doing is right. Steady weights are a good sign.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Echo review / diuretic follow-up

S: Two weeks on furosemide 40 and KCl 20. Taking both every morning, no missed doses. Urinating a lot until noon, no dizziness or cramps. Breathing about the same as at her first visit: still stops halfway up the stairs at work. Still sleeps propped up. Home weights 63.0-63.6 kg, steady. Keeping salt down, cooking at home.

O: BP 120/81, HR 78 regular, SpO2 97% RA, wt 63.6 kg.
Lungs clear. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble in left lateral decubitus as before. No edema.

TTE 5/9 (regional hospital echo lab): thickened, doming mitral leaflets with narrowed orifice, MVA 1.2 cm² by planimetry, mean gradient 9 mmHg, LA enlarged, no significant MR, aortic valve normal. LV normal size/wall thickness/function, EF 60%, LVEDP estimated normal. PASP estimated 45 mmHg.

A/P:
1. Rheumatic heart disease with severe mitral stenosis. Fits the childhood rheumatic fever and the exam. Spent a long time explaining the valve to her with a drawing. Added to problem list.
- Cardiology referral placed today, echo and ECG to go with it.
2. Chronic heart failure due to the mitral stenosis, NYHA class III: comfortable at rest, symptoms with less than ordinary activity. LV function preserved, the problem is the valve. Added to problem list.
- Continue furosemide 40 mg daily and KCl 20 mEq daily.
- BMP today.
- 2 g sodium, daily weights. Call if up more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week, or more short of breath.
3. Elevated estimated PA systolic pressure (45 mmHg) on echo, from the back-pressure of the stenosed valve. Noted; cardiology to weigh in.
4. Health maintenance: FIT kit given. Mammogram and vaccines at her physical.
RTC about 3 months, sooner prn.

Doing her usual. Breathless with one flight of stairs and carrying groceries, no worse since May. Still on 2 pillows, occasional night waking short of breath, maybe once a week. Weighs herself every morning, 63-64 kg on her log. Low salt, has stopped buying pickles and packaged snacks. No chest pain, no palpitations, no swelling. Taking furosemide and potassium daily.

Cardiology consult is on the books for mid-November.

- Rheumatic mitral stenosis, severe, with chronic HF NYHA III: stable. Continue furosemide 40, KCl 20. BMP today.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT, age 52

Interval: no new problems. Breathing unchanged from summer: limited on stairs and hills, fine at her desk. Sleeps on 2 pillows. Weights steady on home log. Taking furosemide and potassium daily. Cardiology in November.

ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, palpitations, syncope, edema, bleeding, bowel change, breast lumps, mood change. 

PMH: rheumatic mitral stenosis (severe) with chronic HF NYHA III; childhood rheumatic fever.
Meds: furosemide 40 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily.
NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

BP 126/81, HR 73, RR 15, T 36.7, SpO2 96%, wt 63.5 kg.
General well. HEENT normal, no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart regular, apical diastolic rumble in left lateral decubitus. Abd benign. Breast exam deferred to mammogram per pt preference. No edema. Skin normal. Mood bright.

PHQ-9: 1.

Prevention:
- Cervical: co-test 2019 normal at prior practice, next due 2024.
- Breast: mammogram 2021 normal, screening mammogram ordered.
- Colon: FIT negative June 2022.
- Hep C and HIV one-time screening sent today.
- Lipids and A1c today (mother with T2DM, South Asian ancestry).
- Vaccines today: influenza, COVID bivalent booster, Tdap (none on record). PCV20 done in August. Shingrix series to start this winter.

A/P: healthy apart from the valve. Continue current meds. Follow-up after cardiology visit.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Department of Medicine. DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received by fax 10/20/2022)

Patient: Anjali Rahman, 52F. Admitted 10/17/2022 via ED. Discharged 10/19/2022.
Admitting/discharge diagnosis: new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, paroxysmal. Background severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with chronic heart failure.

History: Presented to the ED the evening of 10/17 with palpitations that started suddenly that afternoon at work. Known severe rheumatic mitral stenosis (echo 5/2022, MVA 1.2 cm²) on furosemide and potassium; cardiology consult pending as outpatient.
ED: HR 136 irregular, BP 118/76, RR 20, T 36.8, SpO2 96% RA. ECG atrial fibrillation with RVR, no acute ST changes.

Hospital course: Rate controlled with IV metoprolol, then oral metoprolol, consolidated to metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. HR 80s-90s by day 2. She remained in atrial fibrillation; rate controlled, so no cardioversion was attempted. Anticoagulation: atrial fibrillation in the setting of rheumatic mitral stenosis, warfarin is the agent of choice; started warfarin 5 mg daily, INR goal 2.0-3.0. Baseline INR 1.0. hs-troponin I 4 ng/L (normal). TSH 1.8 (normal). K 4.7, Cr 0.86, Hgb 12.9.
Discharge vitals: HR 84 irregular, BP 116/74, SpO2 97% RA.

Discharge condition: stable, in rate-controlled atrial fibrillation.

Discharge medications:
- metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg PO daily (NEW)
- warfarin 5 mg PO every evening (NEW), target INR 2-3
- furosemide 40 mg PO daily (continued)
- potassium chloride ER 20 mEq PO daily (continued)
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within one week for INR check and ongoing INR monitoring. Keep scheduled cardiology appointment. Return for bleeding, chest pain, fainting or worse breathlessness.

Attending hospitalist, Department of Medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after discharge summary received. Home since yesterday. Heart still "a bit uneven" but no racing like Monday. Picked up metoprolol succinate and warfarin from pharmacy, took both. Reviewed: warfarin every evening same time, no ibuprofen/naproxen/aspirin, Tylenol ok, call before any new med or antibiotic. Visit with PCP 10/25 at 11:00 with INR. Pt verbalized understanding.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up; atrial fibrillation; start INR monitoring

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit (TCM). Discharge summary from regional hospital reviewed; admitted 10/17-10/19.

S: Went to the ED 10/17 with sudden palpitations, found in AF with RVR, rate controlled with metoprolol, no cardioversion. Started metoprolol succinate 50 and warfarin 5. Since home: aware of an irregular heartbeat at times but no racing. Breathing back to her usual (stairs slow her). No lightheadedness. No bleeding, no dark stools, no bruising. Taking all four meds. Weights 63-64 kg.

O: BP 121/79, HR 82 irregularly irregular, SpO2 97% RA, wt 63.5 kg.
Lungs clear. Irregularly irregular rhythm, rate controlled; apical diastolic rumble. No edema.

Meds reconciled with discharge list: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg every evening, furosemide 40 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily.

A/P:
1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, new this month, still in AF, rate controlled. Added to problem list. Continue metoprolol succinate 50.
2. Anticoagulation with warfarin, goal INR 2-3 (AF + mitral stenosis). Monitoring here from now on. INR today, our RN will call with dosing.
Warfarin teaching done today with pt: keep vitamin K foods steady week to week rather than avoiding them (she eats a lot of spinach and methi, keep portions consistent), signs of bleeding (black stools, blood in urine, nosebleed that won't stop, unusual bruising, bad headache), no NSAIDs or aspirin, check with us before any new prescription, antibiotic or herbal product. Written handout and INR log given.
3. Rheumatic mitral stenosis, severe, chronic HF NYHA III: stable. BMP today. Continue furosemide/KCl.
4. Cardiology consult 11/14.
RTC 3 months; INR per RN.

documents.title: INR dosing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.7, one week into warfarin: still below her goal of 2.0-3.0 (the lab H flag is against the off-warfarin reference range). Per PCP: take 7.5 mg (1.5 tablets) tonight only, then back to 5 mg every evening. Recheck INR 11/1. Called pt, she repeated instructions back. BMP K 4.5, Cr 0.92.

documents.title: INR
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 2.4, therapeutic. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily. Next INR in 4 weeks, 11/29. Pt informed via portal.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION (letter received 11/17/2022)
Re: Anjali Rahman, DOB 05/03/1970
Seen 11/14/2022 at the request of her primary care physician for severe rheumatic mitral stenosis.

History: 52-year-old woman, emigrated from India about ten years ago, with rheumatic fever as a child (hospitalized, no secondary prophylaxis afterward). Over the past year she has become progressively more breathless with falling exercise tolerance, which led to her presentation to primary care in May and an echocardiogram showing severe mitral stenosis. She describes occasional palpitations. In October she was admitted to a regional hospital for atrial fibrillation of sudden onset, rate controlled and started on warfarin.

Current medicines: warfarin 5 mg nightly (target INR 2-3); furosemide 40 mg each morning; metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg once a day; potassium chloride ER 20 mEq once a day. No known drug allergies.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: vital signs stable, heart rate irregular and below 100. Low-pitched apical diastolic rumble, brought out with her turned onto her left side, and an opening snap just after S2. Bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation.

Office echocardiogram: restricted mitral valve opening, enlarged left atrium; LV size and function normal.
ECG: irregularly irregular rhythm, atrial fibrillation with controlled rate.

Impression:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, NYHA class III symptoms.
2. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, currently in AF with controlled rate, on warfarin.

Plan: no medication changes. Continue warfarin with INR 2.0-3.0, furosemide, metoprolol succinate and potassium chloride. INR monitoring to continue with her primary care office. Follow-up in cardiology clinic.

Attending cardiologist
